message: camelCase class name. BEM names are lower kebab-case: cardTitle becomes card-title.
The element separator is exactly two underscores: card_title becomes card__title.
BEM has no element of an element. card__body__title becomes card__body-title, or a block of its own.
The modifier comes last. card--wide__title becomes card__title with card__title--wide.
A modifier stands alone here. It must ride next to its base class: class="card card--wide".
Attribute name in capitals. The extractor reads a lower-case class= attribute.
Space directly after the opening quote. It becomes an empty selector in the extracted stylesheet.
Scripting hook written with an underscore. Use a hyphen: js_toggle becomes js-toggle.
The same class appears twice in one attribute, so the extracted stylesheet would carry the rule twice.
Presentational class name. Name the role, not the paint: card__title--red becomes card__title--alert.
Placeholder class name still in the markup. It will land in the stylesheet as a real selector.
Class name built by a template expression. The extractor cannot resolve it; write the static block part as a class of its own.
Eight or more classes on one element. The block interface is being replaced by loose utilities.
Five or more words in one BEM name. Split the block; the name is carrying the whole page path.
Inline style on this element. That declaration never reaches the extracted stylesheet, so the block ends up styled in two places.
Class attribute in single quotes. The extractor reads double-quoted attributes.
